title: Next step
content:
The next steps in the development process. Managing css is quite challenging, current approach is to split styles per files and only merege them once site is cemented. Style and presentation seem to be too time consuming. How to streamline those activities?

Some of the next tasks:

> Clipboard catcher enhancements - categories (folder) view

> Gallery enhancements - thumbnails quality (minimize full picture?), admin quick panel governing options e.g. thumnbail type

> Scripts need splitting in general, max for LLM is about 500 lines before they start producing nonsense

> Develop further demos for different styles of layouts, menus (hamburger vs roll-out vs...)

> Developer blogger fix landing after saving post

I guess I need some sort of bambam or whatever board to track... Let's see how goes.

title: I suppose...
content:
...all the demo stuff ought to be moved to demo dedicated stuff, aka playground 1/2. Galant demos start to look somewhat digestible as well. Holiday planner project is the next big one.

A matrix of airlines for example: first which airlines at all connect between locations. Then at what time are the flights. And comments, prices, date of entry as schedules change, some history would nice too always.
A map initially build on a grid of squares basically something like

AXA
SXM/SFM  AGU
   SKB
   
      PTP
      DOM
      FDF
      SLU
         BGI
      SVN
      GND


Something like thata, designing a map module will be too much pita with llm at this stage.


Any such module will require building dedicated json files and gemini provided some code but im highly skeptical and tired of AI vomit. Stuck and magic are two other project. Dont forget was supposed to be the next one. For that we need a checklist manager. For that we need a jason manager. LLM is nice for sandbox stuff but anything more serious is a tedious walk through the valley of frustration before understanding is reached. I guess my prompt-fu is not at the right level but then again cut me some slack. Yeah anything more than 100 lines of code seems to be pretty much guaranteed not to work as soon as any specific requirements arise to general functionality.

Flexibility, robustness are key, any time a new column may be needed, and then some php enhancement. Hence why code is modular but llm needs the big picture explained each and every time and that is quite fatiguing.

Though I suppose at this stage I can ask llm to generate a prompt for llm by reiterating in the llm the code that was generated by llm. What a time to be alive!

PS. What about this blogger what other enhancements could i add.. I guess the text is terribly sterile but html tags are there so I shouldn't bother too much with a GUI for editing. Modals each time are a bit of pita on the other hand we want all of them to look the same which is some sections, window, etc...
